newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean Central Bank to issue new bonds.
newsitem.headline: Chilean Central Bank to issue new bonds.

text.p: The Central Bank of Chile will begin issuing a new 90-day discount bond and a 42-day nominal bond as of July 9, both to be sold by auction, the institution said Friday.

The creation of the instruments is part of capital market reforms made possible by lower inflation rates and is aimed at "transferring a greater role to the market in determining the structure of interest rates," said the Central Bank in a statement.

The first instruments, known in Spanish as "pagares descontables a noventa dias" or PDBC-90, will be issued in pesos and not adjusted for inflation. They will be auctioned on every Tuesday and Thursday together with the 90-day PRBC bonds currently sold on those days by the bank, said the statement.
The amount of the new bonds to be offered will initially be equivalent to 10 percent of the monthly supply of Central Bank short-term bonds, said the statement.

The bank will also eliminate non-auction sales of 30-day PDBC bonds and end the publication of a periodic "inflation signal," which gives a forecast of consumer inflation for the month along with sales of the 30-day bond.

Instead, the bank will issue a 42-day bond not adjusted for inflation, the PDBC-42, to be sold through auctions on Wednesdays, it said. The total amount of the new 42-day bond will be between three and five billion pesos per session, said the bank.
